page: Amazon Web Services r7a.xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor, which operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the top 25% tier. Text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also show strong results. However, multi-core performance, software compilation, and database operations reside in the average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks, which registers in the bottom 25% tier at 37.49 GB/sec, contrasted against average cached small-block read bandwidth of 592.0 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference speeds are also weak, with a 7B model achieving only 23.33 tokens/sec for prompt processing.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7a.xlarge offers high DDR5 memory density and dedicated CPU allocation without the added cost of bundled local storage or GPUs. This makes it a balanced option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-speed local disk access. The instance is suitable for in-memory caching, medium-scale database operations, text processing, and general-purpose workloads requiring a high memory footprint relative to compute capacity.
